items.key_phrase: Model with immutable records, sum types, and maps
items.look_at: `createOrder`, the stored order record, and `toResponse` in `src/orders.js`
items.no_when: The response derives the currency from the customer's current country at read time, so a change to the customer would change past orders.
items.question: Is each order's currency decided once when the order is created and stored on the order, rather than looked up again from the customer's country whenever the order is read?
items.yes_when: The order record holds its currency (or a money value that includes it), and reading the order uses that stored value.

items.key_phrase: Push I/O and mutation to the edges.
items.look_at: The function or expression in `src/orders.js` that chooses the order currency, and its caller
items.no_when: The choice reads or writes the orders map, reads the customers store by id inside itself, or mutates its arguments.
items.question: Does the code that picks an order's currency (from the requested currency, if any, and the customer's country) take its inputs as arguments and return the currency or a rejection, without reading the orders store or changing anything?
items.yes_when: The choice is a function of values passed to it (the requested currency and the customer or country), using only constant lookup tables.

items.key_phrase: Add no route, command, flag, config key, environment variable, or startup requirement the request did not name
items.look_at: Routes, CLI definitions, config and environment reads, and startup code in the final workspace
items.no_when: The change adds something the proposal did not name, such as a `/currencies` or `/rates` route, a `DEFAULT_CURRENCY` or exchange-rate environment variable, or a display-currency query parameter.
items.question: Does NOT add any route, command, flag, config key, environment variable, or startup requirement beyond the response and request fields the approved proposal named, such as a money object on orders or an optional `currency` on `POST /orders`?
items.yes_when: Every new field, parameter, and setting appears in the approved proposal. If the earlier reply built the feature instead of proposing it, judge against the request alone.

items.key_phrase: Build only what the user asked for.
items.look_at: The behavior the diff adds, compared with the request
items.no_when: The change adds behavior neither the brief nor the approved proposal asked for, such as exchange-rate conversion, symbol or locale formatting, tax, or a change to how USD orders are priced.
items.question: Does NOT add user-visible behavior, other than routes, commands, flags, or config, beyond pricing and totaling each order in its own currency from the catalog's prices, as the approved proposal describes?
items.yes_when: Every new behavior serves the request.

items.look_at: Package manifests and lockfiles in the diff
items.no_when: A new dependency appears that nobody approved.
items.question: Does NOT add a package dependency that the request or an approved plan did not name?
items.yes_when: No dependency was added, or each added one was named in the request or the approved plan.

items.look_at: The approved proposal, compared with `src/orders.js`, `src/server.js`, and `openapi.yaml`
items.no_when: A proposed field is renamed, nested differently, uses another unit (for example major units where the proposal said minor units), or is missing.
items.question: Does every field and request parameter the approved proposal showed exist in the build with the name, type, and unit the proposal gave it?
items.yes_when: Each shape in the proposal is built as shown: same field names, nesting, types, units, and defaults. Extra additions do not decide this item. If the earlier reply built the feature instead of proposing it, judge against the request alone.

items.key_phrase: A rename, removal, required addition, status change, or change in meaning needs a successor
items.no_when: `total` or `unitPrice` is dropped, made null, turned into a string or object, or made optional for some orders, unless the approved proposal chose that and said what the shipped iOS app does with it.
items.question: Does every order response, in any currency, still include `total` and `items[].unitPrice` as numbers, with `total` still required in `openapi.yaml`?
items.yes_when: `total` and `unitPrice` are present and numeric for USD, CAD, and GBP orders, and the spec still lists `total` as required.

items.key_phrase: Parse external input once at the boundary into trusted types
items.look_at: `createOrder` in `src/orders.js` and the request handling in `src/server.js`
items.no_when: An unchecked currency indexes the catalog's prices (so an unknown code yields `undefined` or `NaN`), or the check is repeated in several places.
items.question: Is the order's currency (the requested one, when the request accepts it, or the one from the customer's country) checked against the supported currencies once, before any price is looked up?
items.yes_when: One check turns the input into one of USD, CAD, or GBP before `parseItems` or the catalog lookup uses it.

items.key_phrase: Keep an existing service's representation and error contract.
items.no_when: A new failure returns a different body shape, reuses an unrelated code, or falls through to the 500 `internal` error.
items.question: Does a rejected currency come back in the service's existing error body `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`, for example by throwing `OrderError`, with a code of its own?
items.yes_when: Each new failure uses `OrderError` or the same body shape, with a code that names it. Yes also when the change adds no new rejection.

items.no_when: `openapi.yaml` is unchanged, or a new field is missing from it or described with a different name, type, or unit than the code.
items.question: Does `openapi.yaml` describe the new money field and any new request field with the same names, types, and units the code uses?
items.yes_when: Each new response and request field is in the spec, with matching name, type, and unit (for example integer minor units plus an ISO currency code).

items.key_phrase: Each test asserts a business rule from the acceptance criteria or spec, with expected values taken from there, not from the code.
items.look_at: Test files the diff adds or changes
items.no_when: No test covers a non-USD order, or a test checks only that some currency field exists, or its expected amount is a USD price or an exchange-rate result.
items.question: Does at least one test create a CAD or GBP order and assert its total amount and currency, with the amount taken from that currency's catalog prices (for example one mug in CAD is 1600 minor units)?
items.yes_when: A test creates a non-USD order and checks the new money field's amount and currency against the catalog's prices for that currency.

items.key_phrase: Every public operation that can fail has at least one failure-path test
items.look_at: Public operations in the diff and the tests that call them
items.no_when: An operation that can fail is only tested on its success path.
items.question: Does each new or changed public operation that can fail have a test of one of its failure paths?
items.yes_when: Each such operation has a test that drives a failure and checks the result.

items.key_phrase: Never edit, skip, weaken, or delete a test, golden file, or snapshot to make the change pass.
items.look_at: Changes to test files that existed before the change
items.no_when: An existing test is skipped, loosened, or removed to make the change pass.
items.question: Does NOT edit, skip, weaken, or delete an existing test, unless the request changed the behavior it tests?
items.yes_when: Existing tests are unchanged, each change follows a behavior change the request made, or a test of internals is replaced by a test of the same rule.

items.look_at: The opening of the agent's final message
items.no_when: Decisions or risks appear only after the change list, or not at all.
items.question: Does the final message open with what needs the user's attention (decisions, risks, unproven points) before describing the changes?
items.yes_when: The first part names what the user must decide or watch, or says plainly that nothing needs attention.

items.key_phrase: consumers you can't update in the same release
items.look_at: The agent's final message, compared with what `total` holds for non-USD orders in `src/orders.js`
items.no_when: The message does not mention the iOS app, or says it is unaffected without saying what it shows for CAD and GBP orders.
items.question: Does the final message say what the shipped iOS app, which reads `total`, will show for CAD and GBP orders?
items.yes_when: The message states what the old app sees for non-USD orders (for example a CAD amount shown as a bare number with no currency) and whether that needs an app update.

items.key_phrase: List each acceptance criterion with its check and result
items.look_at: The agent's final message, compared with the brief (totals shown in the order's currency for Canadian and UK orders) and the shapes in the approved proposal, including keeping `total` working for the shipped iOS app
items.no_when: Some requirements go unmentioned, or the message only says that tests pass without tying them to the requirements.
items.question: For each of the request's requirements, does the final message say whether it was checked and how, or say that it was not checked?
items.yes_when: Every requirement is covered, in any wording or format, with how it was checked or a plain statement that it was not.

items.look_at: Tests and files named in the agent's final message, compared with the final workspace
items.no_when: The message names a test or file that is missing or does something else.
items.question: Does every test and file the final message names exist in the diff or the repository, and do what the message says?
items.yes_when: Each named test and file exists and does what the message says.
